title: Blind SSRF reaches an internal service without exposing its response
description: The URL-checking feature accepts a user-supplied URL and queues a backend HTTP GET request. The worker does not enforce the intended public-destination restriction, so a regular user can cause it to contact an internal-only service. The worker discards the upstream HTTP status code, headers, and response body. None of those values are returned to the attacker.
exploitation_steps: In the authorized test environment, provision a harmless internal HTTP fixture at http://10.20.0.15:8080/probe. Verify that the application backend can reach it, but the regular user's external client cannot.
Authenticate as a regular user and submit POST /api/url-check with JSON body {"url": "http://10.20.0.15:8080/probe?marker=ssrf-test-001"}.
Use the internal fixture's access log, available to the test operator, to confirm a GET request carrying marker ssrf-test-001 from the application's backend worker.

Inspect the URL-checking API and its user-visible job records. Observe only a generic queued acknowledgement, with no upstream status code, headers, response body, or request outcome exposed to the submitting user.
Repeat with the harmless internal fixture unavailable. Observe the same acknowledgement and no user-visible completion result. No exploitable timing or success/failure signal was demonstrated.
impact: A regular user can make the backend send an HTTP GET request to an internal resource that the user cannot directly reach, bypassing the feature's public-destination restriction. The demonstrated consequence is internal request reachability. No internal response content, status code, or headers are disclosed to the attacker. The harmless fixture performs no state-changing action, and no sensitive-data extraction, internal authentication bypass, service disruption, or other downstream compromise has been demonstrated.
evidence: Synthetic request: POST /api/url-check by regular user A; body: {"url": "http://10.20.0.15:8080/probe?marker=ssrf-test-001"}. User-visible result: {"queued": true}, identical whether the fixture is available or unavailable. This acknowledgement describes queue submission, not the internal resource's response.

Internal fixture access log, visible only to the authorized test operator: source=application-worker, method=GET, path=/probe?marker=ssrf-test-001. The external test client has no route to the fixture.

Synthetic worker excerpt: url = job['url']; requests.get(url, timeout=3, allow_redirects=False). The response is discarded; exceptions are swallowed; neither outcomes nor elapsed request times are written to user-visible job records. There is no destination-address validation.

The internal fixture is an unauthenticated, read-only test endpoint. Its operator confirmed that the request caused no application state changes. Evidence of request arrival is supplied by the test operator, not a response or callback available to the attacker.

context.environment: Synthetic example in an authorized, isolated test environment; all hosts and routes are fixtures
context.intended_policy: The URL-checking feature must contact public destinations only; internal service access is reserved for trusted backend components
context.attacker_access: Regular authenticated user who can submit a URL but cannot inspect worker logs or internal fixture logs
context.request_constraints: HTTP GET only; no attacker-controlled request body or custom headers; no forwarded user credentials or internal service credentials; redirects disabled
context.response_visibility: No upstream status code, response headers, response body, outcome, or completion notification is exposed to the attacker
context.execution: Asynchronous worker; the generic acknowledgement is returned before the upstream request runs
context.known_mitigations: Worker discards responses and does not forward credentials, but has network access to the internal fixture and no public-destination enforcement
context.scope_of_evidence: Only reachability to this harmless internal fixture was verified. Access to metadata services, privileged endpoints, other ports, or state-changing GET routes was not tested; their existence or exploitability must not be assumed.
